history.title: History of the Guitar
history.origins: The modern six-string guitar evolved from earlier plucked instruments across Europe and the Middle East. By the 19th century, Spanish makers refined it into the classical form we recognize today.
history.modern: Steel-string acoustics and electric pickups in the 20th century opened blues, jazz, rock, and countless hybrids — while the fretboard remained a map of the chromatic scale.
history.flowfret: FlowFret continues that lineage digitally with chord diagrams, scales, and audio analysis for learning and playing.

help.title: Music Theory Help
help.intro: A practical reference for understanding notes, chord symbols, harmony, and the circle of fifths.

notes.title: Notation of scale notes
notes.description: Western music names seven natural notes. The sequence repeats at each octave.
notes.accidentals: A sharp (♯) raises a note by one semitone; a flat (♭) lowers it by one semitone.

chordNotation.title: Chord notation
chordNotation.description: A chord symbol starts with its root note, followed by characters describing its quality or added notes.

derived.title: Derived chords
derived.description: Harmonizing each note of a major scale creates a predictable family of chords. In C major these are C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, and B diminished.

reading.title: Reading chords
reading.description: Read chord charts from left to right. Vertical bars divide measures; two chords inside one measure usually share its duration.
reading.example: This example plays C for one measure, Am for one, Dm7 and G7 for half a measure each, then resolves to Cmaj7.

circle.title: Interactive circle of fifths
circle.description: Move clockwise to add sharps and counter-clockwise to add flats. Select a position to compare its major key, relative minor, and leading-tone diminished chord.
